<!-- Slide number: 4 -->
Identifier scheme
| Prefix | Meaning | Stated in |
| --- | --- | --- |
| BR-nn | Business requirement | Business requirements |
| FR-nn | Functional requirement | User stories |
| NFR-nn | Non-functional requirement | Non-functional requirements |
| REG-nn | Regulatory obligation | Regulatory requirements |
| C-nn | Constraint (requirements) / Control (governance) | Business requirements / control matrix |
| A-nn | Assumption (requirements) / Action (postmortem) | Business requirements / postmortem |
| G-nn | Known regulatory gap | Regulatory requirements |
| T-nn | Test finding | Traceability matrix |
| R-nn | Risk | Risk register |
| W-nn | Waiver | Release plan |

### Notes:
Identifiers are the thread through the whole set. A requirement is named where it is stated, where it is designed, where it is implemented, and where it is tested.

Following one identifier across the set is the quickest way to read it. BR-05 is a good one: stated in the business requirements, designed as an append-only consent table, implemented in services/consent.py, fully tested there, claimed as control C-09 in the HIPAA matrix — and never consulted by the export path, which is how it became T-03, then W-01, then R-01.
Full table has 10 rows; 10 shown.

<!-- Slide number: 5 -->
The state of this release, honestly

### Notes:
Release 1.0.0 shipped on 2026-06-04 with three high-severity findings open under a single bundled waiver. One of them caused INC-2026-0814 six weeks later. Two are still open, and one of those two — the consent check — is a control the governance documentation claims and the software does not contain.

That is not a failure of any individual document. Each phase produced what it was supposed to produce, and the gap was written down every time. It was carried forward because nobody read the four documents together at the moment the decision was made.

items.text:
Monday was quiet until the referral queue backed up around 14:00.
The coordinator dashboard showed 41 open referrals, most from Northvale.
Restarting the worker cleared the queue but nobody knows why it stalled.
Owner for the follow-up is TBD.
Tuesday the nightly export ran long again and finished at 06:40.
The risk scores were stale for the morning huddle.
We agreed to look at the export schedule but the new time is TBD.
Wednesday there was a short outage of the patient search page.
It matched the pattern from the August incident but recovered by itself.
Somebody should check whether the connection pool fix is deployed. TODO.
Thursday was uneventful apart from two password resets.
Friday the clinic in Eastfield reported slow page loads after 16:00.
The network team said there was maintenance on their side.
Saturday and Sunday had no pages.
Next week we expect the Northvale data feed change to go live.
The rollback plan for that change is to be confirmed.
Please read the deployment runbook before Thursday.
Questions go to the platform channel.

items.label: review
items.text:
Present: Amara (clinical lead), Jonas (engineering), Wei (records team)
Apologies: Dr Patel

1. Consent export defect. Jonas said the fix is ready for review. Agreed it ships only after Wei signs off the audit wording.
2. Pilot ward rollout. Amara asked to move the start to 3 March. Agreed.
3. Open risks. Nothing new raised.

Decided: the release waits for the consent fix. Jonas to circulate the test evidence by Friday; Wei to confirm the audit wording by Monday.

items.label: postmortem
items.text:
On Tuesday the referral service stopped accepting new referrals for 47 minutes.

09:12 the nightly certificate rotation replaced the database client certificate.
09:14 the first referral submissions failed with a TLS handshake error.
09:31 the on-call engineer was paged by the error-rate alert.
09:59 the previous certificate was restored and submissions recovered.

The rotation job had never been run against the referral database, because it was added to the rotation list after the last test. 212 referrals were rejected and resubmitted by ward staff by hand.

We will add the referral database to the rotation test (owner Jonas, by 14 March) and alert on certificate expiry 14 days ahead (owner Wei, by 21 March).

items.label: release_notes
items.text:
CarePath 2.4 is available from today.

Clinicians can now see where a referral is once it leaves their ward, and the referral list can be filtered by receiving clinic.
The patient search no longer times out for surnames shared by more than 500 patients.
Exports to partner organisations now check the patient's consent first, and an export without consent is refused and recorded.

Nothing needs to be done to upgrade: the change was applied overnight. If a referral looks wrong, call the service desk on extension 4400.

items.label: risk_register
items.text:
Things that could stop the pilot, as of February:

- The community clinics may not have scanners by March. Fairly likely; it would delay the pilot a month. Amara is chasing the order.
- Medical record numbers might not be unique across the network. Unlikely, but referrals would be filed against the wrong patient. Wei is checking a sample.
- The partner export could ship before consent is checked. We have seen it happen once; it would be a reportable breach. Jonas owns the fix, now in test.
